XCOM discovers the high likelihood of an Alien Base hidden somewhere on Earth after capturing an Outsider Shard. After studying the shard, XCOM is able to identify a communication frequency that allows them locate the underground base; the Alien Base is located on a random continent for each game. In addition to serving as a command and control center and supply depot for the invaders, the Aliens have been transferring abducted humans here to experiment on them.

Aim in XCOM: Enemy Unknown and XCOM: Enemy Within is a unit attribute and gameplay mechanic. Aim is a measurement of a unit's accuracy when firing a weapon, and is directly related to one's chance of successfully hitting a target. It does not affect melee attacks, area of effect weapons (such as grenades and rocket launchers), or offensive abilities. Each point of Aim is equivalent to 1% accuracy.

ADVENT MECs are enemies encountered in XCOM 2. They are large autonomous mechanical units that provide heavy support for other ADVENT units. ADVENT MECs are the first robotic enemies in the game, and can rival ADVENT Officers in terms of combat effectiveness. MECs are the first enemies to wear armor, allowing them to take reduced damage to all attacks, sufficing for explosives or shredding rounds. However, This is where their defenses end, as they lack the ability to dodge, take cover, and can be shut down or even commandeered by an experienced XCOM Specialist. An E.X.O. Suit is a heavy armor in XCOM 2. The E.X.O Suit is typically the first heavy armor the player obtains. It provides an extra health and armor point over the Predator Armor, and can mount a single Heavy Weapon, however it does not provide an extra slot for utilities. It can be considered a direct upgrade over the Predator Armor if one of the utility slots used by the soldier is a Frag Grenade; the default Rocket Launcher does more damage and grants the soldier extra durability.

Dazed is a mental status effect in XCOM 2: War of the Chosen. __TOC__ Similarly to Stunned, dazed disables a unit's ability to act. Dazed can be inflicted by all of the Chosen. The dazed units can be abducted for interrogation (a unit is captured and removed from the battlefield), or the Chosen can extract information from them immediately (a unit stays on the battlefield and dazed is removed). After performing either of these actions, the Chosen will leave the battlefield . Once the Chosen is defeated or killed, the dazed effect is removed from all XCOM soldiers.

The Alien Fortress Assault, codenamed Operation Leviathan, is the final storyline mission of XCOM 2. The Commander must make their way to the Psi Gate at the end of a map, defeat the 3 Avatars controlled by the Elders, and keep the Commander's Avatar alive to complete the mission. The Commander must defeat all 3 Avatars to destroy the Avatar Project once and for all.

Alien Facility Assaults are critical, non-plot driven missions in XCOM 2. These missions are dedicated to destroying the Alien Facility and delaying the Avatar Project. Alien Facilities are signified with a bright red triangular logo and the ADVENT logo on the Geoscape. If successful, the Doom Counter will be set back by however many bars of progress the facility had contributed to it. For example, if the Facility had contributed 5 pips, the progress will be reduced by 5. It is not important to neutralize all enemies, but the X4 charges must be placed at the designated area. Epic Weapons are unique equipment that can be acquired by spending roughly 100-120 Intel in the Scavenger Market when they appear, or as rewards from City 31 Missions. Epic Weapons have the same damage of other weapons of their type, including increases from weapon enhancement upgrades.
City 31 is the main setting for the story events of XCOM: Chimera Squad.

An Assembly is machinery that manufactures equipment. Assemblies can function autonomously but benefit from active monitoring. Their use is highly controlled because of their potentially dangerous applications. The use of unshackled Assemblies, which are capable of producing weaponry, is especially restricted. Chimera Squad may encounter a mission where they have to destroy an unshackled Assembly used by hostiles who are attempting to print and detonate a bomb. In another mission, Chimera Squad must stop Gray Phoenix from using an Assembly to build homemade plasma missiles. Air and Space is one of five continent bonuses available in XCOM: Enemy Unknown. It is unlocked by either placing XCOM headquarters in North America at the beginning of a new game, or by placing satellites in orbit over all three North American countries during the game.

All In is one of five continent bonuses available in XCOM: Enemy Unknown. It is unlocked by either placing XCOM headquarters in Africa at the beginning of a new game, or by placing satellites in orbit over all three African countries during the game.

The game difficulty in XCOM: Enemy Unknown can be set at one of four levels: Easy, Normal, Classic, or Impossible. Each difficulty setting affects a large number of game parameters creating a significant learning curve between difficulties. The difficulty setting can be changed (up or down) at any point in the game but may affect the player's ability to claim certain achievements.

Mindfray is an ability used by Sectoid Commanders, Ethereals, the Uber Ethereal, and Psionic Class soldiers in XCOM: Enemy Unknown. The formula for the chance of a successful of Mindfray is: Chance of Success = Psi attacker's Will - Target's Will + 40 In particular, the chance of success is independent of cover, distance, aim, etc. This means that a Psionic with at least 70 Will has a guaranteed chance of Mindfraying and instantly killing Floaters and Sectoids with a single attack. Those with at least 75 Will can guarantee killing Thin Men in Classic or lower difficulties.

Personal Combat Sims are neural enhancements that provide battle boosts to soldiers in XCOM 2. A Personal Combat Sim (or PCS) provides a permanent upgrade to a soldier's performance, but a soldier can only utilize a single PCS at a time; a soldier can overwrite their selected PCS at any time with a different or higher-grade PCS, but the previous PCS will be lost (unless you have the Lock and Load continental bonus).

Research is a facility aboard the Avenger in XCOM 2. It is located on the west part of the ship, in it is the elerium core that powers the Avenger. Here the Commander can initiate Research Projects, see the available Research Projects and read the Project Reports. It's lead by Chief Scientific Officer Richard Tygan.

Health is a statistic in XCOM 2 that determines how much damage a unit can take before its death; when a unit's health reaches 0, it dies and can no longer be used. Both Soldiers and Aliens have health, and although Alien health remains static throughout the game, Soldier health can be improved in a number of ways. XCOM Rookie soldiers begin with a total health of 4-5 (depending on difficulty) This can be improved through ranking up, equipping Armor and Armor-based Utilities, or using a Conditioning Personal Combat Sim. This is crucial, as the survivability of a soldier highly depends on how much maximum health they have. There is a chance that an XCOM soldier will become critically wounded
The Psi Amp (psionic amplifier) is a Psi Amp in XCOM 2. It is used by a Psi Operative to cast psionic abilities.

Psi Points is a unit statistic, or attribute, in XCOM 2. The psionic offense of a soldier increases with each ability the soldier learns, and with the level of the Psi-Amp they have equipped. Like the Will stat, Psi Offense grows at a rate of 4-13 per level with a cap of 100, however Psi Offense will always start on 50 at Initiate. This gives around a 50% chance of reaching the cap(avg 50+51 pts). To ensure maximum value, if you have the resources, discard or ignore acolytes with low Psi Offense stat rolls.

Hacking skill is an attribute in XCOM 2. The hacking skill in XCOM 2 is a skill everyone has. It involves a machine, like sectopods, Advent Security Towers, etc. that is hacked by a soldier. Each and every soldier has a tech score. Usually specialists will have higher than average ones. To hack, you need to walk over to the green star tile. Specialists may be able to hack with their Gremlin models from father away. After clicking on it, it will give you two choices of rewards to choose from. Sometimes, a failed hack (where you select a reward that had a percentage that was not reached) will result in a benefit for the hacked unit. There are four lists the XCOM 2 chooses names from: m_aFirstOpName, m_aSecondOpName, m_aFirstOpWord, m_aSecondOpWord. With a probability of 50%, the game chooses the first and the second word from m_aFirstOpName and m_aSecondOpName respectively. Otherwise, the name gets chosen from m_aFirstOpWord and m_aSecondOpWord. In this case, the names might be the same, so a new second word is chosen if needed. In addition, there is a 1/500 chance that the second word will be "Chicken".

Their covering fire and suppression abilities can help control enemy movement on the battlefield.

Second Wave is a free DLC add-on for XCOM: Enemy Unknown that enables players to unlock advanced gameplay options for increased challenge and replayability. Players will have to start a new game to access these modifiers.

The Squaddie rank is the first primary rank of soldiers. A soldier at this rank unlocks the primary ability for their class. To achieve this rank, a Rookie needs about one kill worth of experience. New soldiers start at this rank if the New Guy training is purchased at the Officer Training School.

The Sergeant rank is the third rank available to soldiers. A soldier at this rank unlocks a nickname, in addition to a new ability. Having a soldier at this rank also unlocks Squad Size I and Wet Work for purchase at the Officer Training School.
Rift is an ability used by Ethereals and the Uber Ethereal in XCOM: Enemy Unknown. It is also available to The Volunteer during the game's final assault.

The Zudjari are an alien species and the main antagonists in The Bureau: XCOM Declassified. Dubbed the "Outsiders" by humans, they are the leaders of the 1962 alien invasion of Earth. Zudjari (or just Zudj, in their language) are humanoid in build with distinctive grey to green skin, bald, slanted heads, and a mouth that opens vertically. They are a militaristic, expansive civilization, that invade planets, consume the resources, and enslave the population before moving on; Sectoids are among the races conquered by the Zudjari, while Mutons appear to be hired muscle. XCOM: Enemy Within is an expansion pack for XCOM: Enemy Unknown. It was released on November 12th, 2013 in North America and November 15th 2013 elsewhere. Announced at Gamescom 2013, XCOM: Enemy Within adds new abilities, upgrades, weapons, and a new soldier class to combat new enemy threats. This expansion pack also introduces new resources, new maps, new tactical and strategic gameplay, and new multiplayer content. The squad leader is the core component of a squad of soldiers in XCOM: Enemy Unknown. They are first in the firing order during missions, and their death is likely to induce panic among surviving squad members. The importance of their role is increased in XCOM: Enemy Within. The squad leader is indicated by a yellow star over their rank icon in battle.

Utility Items are available to XCOM soldiers via equipment slots in single player campaign. Most utility items are passive or limited-use items that fulfill a variety of functions from restoring HP to providing concealment. Several utility items are available for instant production in Engineering, while many others become available upon completion of certain research projects or through experimental projects in the Proving Ground. All XCOM soldiers are capable of equipping only a single utility item from the start of a campaign. The War for Liberation is the name given in XCOM: Chimera Squad to the events of the XCOM 2 campaign, when the Commander was reinstated as leader of XCOM in 2035 and led XCOM and allied Resistance networks to overthrow ADVENT and destroy the Elders.

The XCOM 2 campaign covers the events of the War for Liberation, when XCOM rescues the Commander and leads resistance forces in a war to overthrow the occupying ADVENT world government. The campaign's gameplay involves recruiting and training soldiers, sending squads on turn-based tactical combat missions, researching technology, and upgrading soldier equipment and the mobile Avenger base. The player must take specific actions to progress the campaign, including research projects, completing key mission objectives, and building Avenger facilities. A Young Captain's Suffering (Japanese: , Komusume Taichō no Kunan) is a quest in . It can be received from Captain Emmy Leater north of the Military District in Colony 9 once Tephra Cave is accessible after the Mechon attack and Raoul has to be added in the affinity chart. Three Wind Vangs can be found flying above the Spring of Grief. It is the second of four quests given by Emmy Leater. If Reyn is in the active party, he will comment. Upon completion, Emmy Leater may offer A Young Captain's Rise.

Absurd Branches (Japanese: , Abusōdo Buranchi) are collectables in . They can be found around Prison Island, and cannot be traded for. According to their description, they are small branches that attract mice from some unknown place and they are always damp.

The 2nd Lift - GF (Japanese: , Dai-2 Rifuto: 1F) is a location in . It is located on the ground floor of Mechonis Field. The party discovers that the lift is not working, upsetting Riki in particular. The story quest Aiming for the Top is triggered, where the party must activate the lift using the main power switch on that floor. They must then do the same for the other floors.

The Abnormal Brog (Japanese: , Akujiki no Guroggu) is a quest exclusive enemy in . It is a member of the Brog family, and can be found at level 16 on the center island in Raguel Lake on the Bionis' Leg during The Greedy Monster. It will drop a lot of Brog Leg Meat, two of which are needed for Material Quest 1.

Abnormal Clone Barg (Japanese: , Akujiki no Kuron Bōku) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a member of the Barg family, and can be found at level 77 in the First Sanctum of Prison Island. It is significantly larger than other Bargs. The Abnormal Clone Barg has a topple spike that inflicts Daze. This spike can be temporarily removed by arts that inflict Aura Seal, such as Monado Purge or Mind Blast.

The 1st Turbine Room (Japanese: , Dai-1 Tābin-shitsu) is a location in . It is located on the first basement floor of Galahad Fortress, directly south of the Main Control Room. The Glacier Acon can be found here, along with an Ether Crystal deposit which contains Strength Up III and Bind Resist III crystals.

The 2nd Lift - 1F (Japanese: , Dai-2 Rifuto: 2F) is a location in . It is located on the first floor of Mechonis Field, north of the 1F Main Power Switch. A Memory 925 Piece can be found here, needed for The History of Mechonis. An Ether Crystal deposit containing Confuse Resist IV and Lock-On Resist IV crystals can also be found here.

The 4F Main Power Switch (Japanese: , 5F Shudengen Kukaku) is a landmark in . It is located on the fourth floor of Mechonis Field, below the west end of the Upper Bulkhead Bridge. Although there are no enemies at the landmark itself, the Revolutionary Bifrons and the Infernal Crocell, both Unique Monsters, can be found near here.
The 2F Observation Post (Japanese: , 3F: Kanshijo) is a location in . It is located on the second floor of Mechonis Field. The Destroyer Salvacion can be found here.
A Snowy Hot Spring (Japanese: , Nengan no Yukimi Onsen damo) is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located at Jakt Geyser on Valak Mountain, between Riki and Shulk at purple affinity.

46-:ri9 is a track in Xenoblade Chronicles X, composed and arranged by Hiroyuki Sawano. It is track 11 of disc three from the XenobladeX Original Soundtrack. This music is heard while the party is in Sylvalum. is unusual among continent background music in that the "day" version of the music is softer and calmer than the "night" version.

The Administrative District (Japanese: , Bureido Eria) is a region in . It is located in central and eastern New Los Angeles. This region corresponds to the BLADE quarters exterior. It is largely on a raised deck, placing it above the rest of New Los Angeles, with the Skell maintenance hangar on the lower deck. The East Gate out of the city is located in this district.

A Challenger Approaches (Japanese: , Kyōryoku, Cooperation) is an Affinity Mission in . It can be received from the BLADE Barracks, near the console. The mission features the first incidents of the alliance between the Humans and Wrothians. Completing this mission unlocks the Six Stars Arms Manufacturer and further Wrothian-related missions. In the , it allows Ga Jiarg to be recruited as a party member.

3D Printers (Japanese: , Rittai Shutsuryokuki ) are unique collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Noctilum, in particular near FN Sites 201, 206 and 210. Four of them are needed for Productivity Power-Up.

The Abyss Reservoir (Japanese: , Shin'en no Dōteiko) is an Unexplored Territory in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located at the bottom of the Cavernous Abyss in Sylvalum, and can only be reached by flying in from above. The Gorkwa can be found here during Child of Mira.

The Abandoned Bivouac (Japanese: , Yaei Atochi) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Cauldros, north of the FN Site 509. There is a teleporter here that leads to the Forgotten Mining Frigates directly above the FN Site 509.

A Fateful Choice (Japanese: , Orufe no Sentaku, The Orphean Choice) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received from On'tonam in the Residential District of New Los Angeles. This mission requires defeating Telethia, the Endbringer, the most powerful Tyrant in the game, for one of its routes.

A Couple of Troublemakers is a Squad Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is part of BLADE Mission No.7, and is unlocked if the Sylooth's weak point is broken during Flying Boulders. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.

The 7th Division (Japanese: , Bundan'sareta Dai Nanaku) is a Location in . It is located on the Streets of the Land of Morytha, beyond the Wall Power Control Room. There is a Treasure Trove here, and a fallen signpost leads to a small area with another Treasure Trove.

50 Volt Batteries are Key Items in . Some of them are obtainable from the Merc Mission Energy for Remodeling. One can be used to put energy into the charging device at Tora's House by filling the gauge by 30% during the quest Powered-Up Poppi.

A Tora and Poppi Production is a Heart-to-Heart in . It can be found in Mymoma Playhouse in Fonsa Myma, Kingdom of Uraya. In order to unlock the Heart-to-Heart, the party must stay at Folmarie Inn once after their story-related stay, after which a dialogue will signal its availability. Completing the Heart-to-Heart increases Nia's and Poppi α's Trust by 100 points.

Acquiring Rare Parts is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Empire of Mor Ardain, and is unlocked automatically when the nation reaches 4 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 100 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 25 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Industry Mastery", "Fortitude" and "Salvaging Mastery" Field Skills.
A Test of Strength is a quest in . It can be received from Yew in Garfont Village in the Kingdom of Uraya.

AC Accuracy Up is an Arts Card in . It grants Poppi the Accuracy Up Blade Art, which increases Tora's accuracy by 25% for 15 seconds. It has a base 75% chance to be used any time Tora misses an attack. Higher ranks reduce the cooldown time of the art. It can be used to customize Poppi α, Poppi QT and Poppi QTπ's supportive capabilities. Poppi QTπ starts equipped with the rank I variant of this Arts Card by default. __TOC__

AC Aggro Draw is an Arts Card in . It grants Poppi the Draw Aggro Blade Art, which increases Tora's current volatile aggro for all enemies by a large amount. This amount increases alongside Tora's level. It has a base 75% chance to be used for every 3 seconds that another party member remains targeted by the enemy. Higher ranks reduce the cooldown time of the art. It can be used to customize Poppi α, Poppi QT and Poppi QTπ's supportive capabilities. Poppi QT starts equipped with the rank I variant of this Arts Card by default. __TOC__

AC Arts Boost is an Arts Card in . It grants Poppi the Arts Plus Blade Art, which increases the damage of the next Art that Tora uses by 50%. It has a base 50% chance to be used any time an Art becomes fully recharged. Higher ranks reduce the cooldown time of the art. It can be used to customize Poppi α, Poppi QT and Poppi QTπ's supportive capabilities. Poppi QTπ starts equipped with the rank I variant of this Arts Card by default. __TOC__

AC Critical Up is an Arts Card in . It grants Poppi the Critical Up Blade Art, which increases Tora's Critical Hit Rate by 25% for 15 seconds. It has a base 75% chance to be used any time one of Tora's Auto-Attacks does not inflict a Critical Hit. Higher ranks reduce the cooldown time of the art. It can be used to customize Poppi α, Poppi QT and Poppi QTπ's supportive capabilities. __TOC__

AC Reaction Nullify is an Arts Card in . It grants Poppi the Nullify Reaction Blade Art, which nullifies the next reaction (Break, Topple, Launch, Smash, Knockback and Blowdown) that is inflicted on Tora in a 15 second window. It has a base 75% chance to be used when Tora is afflicted with a reaction. While the art is capable of nullifying the next reaction and prevent an enemy Driver Combo from progresing, it will not help Tora recover from the current reaction any faster. Higher ranks reduce the cooldown time of the art. It can be used to customize Poppi α, Poppi QT and Poppi QTπ's supportive capabilities. Poppi α starts equipped with the rank I variant of this Arts Card by default. __TOC_

AC Recharge Boost is an Arts Card in . It grants Poppi the Recharge Boost Blade Art, which increases Tora's Recharge rate by 50% for 15 seconds, boosting recharge earned from all effects and actions. It has a base 50% chance to be used any time any time Tora uses a Driver Art and consumes its recharge gauge. Higher ranks reduce the cooldown time of the art. It can be used to customize Poppi QT and Poppi QTπ's supportive capabilities. Poppi α is not compatible with this part. Poppi QT starts equipped with the rank I variant of this Arts Card by default. __TOC__

AC System Reset is an Arts Card in . It grants Poppi the Debuff Cancel Blade Art, which cures all debuffs currently inflicted on Tora. It applies to Doom, Nullify Heal, Shackle Driver, Stench and Taunt. It has a base 50% chance to be used for every 3 seconds that Tora remains afflicted by a debuff. Higher ranks reduce the cooldown time of the art. It can be used to customize Poppi α, Poppi QT and Poppi QTπ's supportive capabilities. __TOC__

AC Back Attack Up is an Arts Card in . It grants Poppi the Back Attack Up Blade Art, which increases the damage of Tora's back attacks by 50% and halves aggro generated for 15 seconds. It has a base 75% chance to be used for every 3 seconds that pass while the buff isn't active. Higher ranks reduce the cooldown time of the art. It can be used to customize Poppi α, Poppi QT and Poppi QTπ's supportive capabilities. __TOC__

AC Damage Absorb is an Arts Card in . It grants Poppi the Absorb Damage Blade Art, which grants Tora a damage barrier of 10% of his maximum HP. This barrier protects him until the cumulative amount of damage has been nullified, at which point it dissipates. It has a base 50% chance to be used any time Tora is hit by an attack. Higher ranks reduce the cooldown time of the art. It can be used to customize Poppi α and Poppi QTπ's supportive capabilities. Poppi QT is not compatible with this part. Poppi QTπ starts equipped with the rank I variant of this Arts Card by default. __TOC__
Adept Attack Gems are an unused Key Item in . They would have unlocked the ability to craft certain gems, but as all gems can be crafted immediately, they are not used in-game.
Adept Defense Gems are an unused Key Item in . They would have unlocked the ability to craft certain gems, but as all gems can be crafted immediately, they are not used in-game.
Adept Healing Gems are an unused Key Item in . They would have unlocked the ability to craft certain gems, but as all gems can be crafted immediately, they are not used in-game.
Adept Assorted Gems are an unused Key Item in . They would have unlocked the ability to craft certain gems, but as all gems can be crafted immediately, they are not used in-game.

A Life Overflowing is a track from , composed by Yasunori Mitsuda. It is track twelve of disc six from the Xenoblade 3 Original Soundtrack, and track twelve of disc seventeen from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. This song plays during the following moments: * When Mio lashes out at O and P. * When Mio talks with Noah the night before her Homecoming Ceremony. * Mio and Noah's discussion about M's intentions in Chapter 6. * When the party returns the belongings of Yew, Zuo, and Heewa to the City during Vandham's Heir. * When Fiona has conflicting emotions when trying to move on from Irma at the end of Transparent Dreams. * When Triton brings the Bright Fig to the Remembrance Sto

A Life Become Distant is a track in and , composed by Yasunori Mitsuda and Mariam Abounnasr. It is track four of disc five from the Xenoblade 3 Original Soundtrack, and track four of disc sixteen from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. This song plays during the following moments in : * When Mio breaks down over her limited time remaining to live. * As the party flees Keves Castle at the beginning of Chapter 5. * Monica's explanation of the City's conservative faction at the Memorial Hall. * During the flashback of two of the previous incarnations of Noah and Mio falling in battle against Z. * During the flashback of Mio brushing off Miyabi when asked about her Flute playing duri
2S-FIELD is a track in , composed by Misaki Umase. This song plays in Volitaris. This song also does not get overwritten by either Don't worry or Don't worry [2XDv] when flying in a Skell.
Alcamoth, or the Imperial Capital Alcamoth (Japanese: , Kōto Akamōto, alt. Imperial City Achamoth; English dub: ), is an area in .

Aged Chilkin Hairs are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by Chilkins on Valak Mountain, and three are required to complete A Token of Friendship. According to their description, they are 100-year old Chilkin ponytails that are often used for cleaning in small spaces.

Ageless Moabit (Japanese: , Furō no Moabīto) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Nebula family, and can be found at level 75 on the ground floor of Prison Island, around the Damaged Transporter.
Aerial Cloak (Japanese: , Hikō Meisai) is a Gem in that reduces the detection range of flying enemies by a percentage. __TOC__

Agility Down (Japanese: , Subayasa Daun) is a Gem in that grants a chance to lower an enemy's Agility when auto-attacking. The gem's activation rate depends on its rank, and can be further increased by Weapon Power gems. __TOC__

This quest will expire after the events at the Mechonis Core. Agniratha Beautification 1 (Japanese: , Agunirāta Bika Sono 1) is a Timed Quest in . It can be received from the City Planning Terminal at the Central Tower in Agniratha. All the quests in Agniratha must be completed in order to get the Cloister Key from the Capital Control Terminal to enter the Seven Sage Cloister.

This quest will expire after the events at the Mechonis Core. Agniratha Beautification 2 (Japanese: , Agunirāta Bika Sono 2) is a Timed Quest in . It can be received from the City Planning Terminal at the Central Tower in Agniratha. All the quests in Agniratha must be completed in order to get the Cloister Key from the Capital Control Terminal to enter the Seven Sage Cloister.

Ageshu Meat Cuts are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can only be dropped by two types of Ageshus on Prison Island. Ageshu Meat Cuts are not otherwise available. According to their description, they are slightly grotesque lumps of meat and tasty steaks can be made out of them.

]] The Aerial Cam is a small device featured in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is known as the Hopper Cam in the Japanese version. It is a flying camera tool that allows players to observe the surrounding terrain from above. It is mainly designed to help players discover routes not seen before. ]]

Alcar's Inferno Eye is a rare material in Xenoblade Chronicles. For unknown reasons, it was cut from the game. It was most likely intended to be dropped by the Dragon King Alcar after it is defeated on Prison Island.

Alcamoth, Imperial Capital (皇都アカモート, Achamoth, Imperial City) is a Field Track in , composed and arranged by Manami Kiyota. It is track 22 of disc 3 from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack. This music is heard during the day in Alcamoth. Motifs from this song are used in "Melia - Ancient Memories" in .

The Alexander Ridge (Japanese: , Arekkusu Sanchi, Alex Mountains) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Oblivia, north of Keegan Ridge. It is bisected by FN Site 315. The Wrothian Stronghold can be accessed from here.
Aetrygons (Japanese: , Derupinu) are flying horned creatures in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Oblivia and Sylvalum.

Aeviter Star Wings are unique materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from the purple Aeviters in Sylvalum. Three of them are needed during The Nopon Heir. They are components in X, XV, and XX Arts: Gain TP and Arts.GP augments.

The Airborne Throne (Japanese: , Kūchū Hōza) is a Secret Area in . It is located on the Upper Level of the Kingdom of Tantal. It can be accessed by traveling past the Lumos Pillar and freezing a bridge to the Pillar City Ruins, then by reaching the top, near Heroic Edwin in a cave, and exiting onto a ledge. There is another gap that needs to be frozen to the left; the party will be assaulted by Incandescent Marcus, then the vines must be climbed. It must be visited to unlock Ursula's level 2 "Fortitude" Field Skill. There is a Treasure Trove here. Azami's heart-to-heart, "A Love Too Deep", can be found here.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Affection Necklaces (Japanese: , Jiai no Kubikazari) are accessories in and . They increase the rate of healing of Recovery-type Arts by up to 19%, boosting their healing power. They are the upgraded version of the Harvest Necklace accessory. The Holy Necklace and Saint's Necklace accessories offer stronger instances of this equipment's effect.

Allies of Justice 3 is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Kingdom of Uraya after completing the mission Allies of Justice 2. The time required to complete this mission is 20 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 5 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Earth Mastery", "Expeditionist" and "Superstrength" Field Skills. This mission unlocks Allies of Justice 4 and the second level of Godfrey's "Justice-Loving Soul" Field Skill.

|-|Aux Core = |-|Skill RAM/Upgrade = Affinity MAX Atk (Japanese: , Kizuna MAX Kōgeki) is an Aux Core or a Skill RAM or Upgrade in and . It increases damage dealt by up to 55% when the Affinity between Driver and Blade is at max. This effect persists until the golden bond dissipates. The Skill RAM/Upgrade variants can be used to customize Poppi QT and Poppi QTπ as an Aux Core equivalent. Poppi α is not compatible with this part. The Magical Pink Pandoria and Mermaid-Blue Pandoria DLC Aux Cores have equivalent effects to this Aux Core's Rank V variant. The Devoted Marigold Nia DLC Aux Core has an equivalent effect to this Aux Core's Rank VI variant. __TOC__

Ahaid Garluses (Japanese: , Ahaido Garuusu) are minor enemies in . They are members of the Garlus family and can be found at level 38 - 44 at Pillar City Ruins on the Upper Level area of Kingdom of Tantal. They are also fought during the Challenge Battle Mode battle Humanoid Alliance.

The Alrest Linkring is a DLC Key Item in . It is obtained from the Nopon Archsage in the Land of Challenge after completing the Challenge Battle Dino Drama. It gives Drivers the ability to equip Shulk and Fiora outside the Land of Challenge, in the world of Alrest, as Blades. The Alrest Link Relay serves the same purpose for Elma.

The Alrest Link Relay is a DLC Key Item in . It is obtained from the Nopon Archsage in the Land of Challenge after completing the Challenge Battle Elma: Redux. It gives Drivers the ability to equip Elma outside the Land of Challenge, in the world of Alrest, as a Blade. The Alrest Linkring serves the same function for Shulk and Fiora.
Agnus Blaster Elites (Japanese: , Agunusu Haifaia) are Minor Enemies in . They are Agnus Soldiers, and can be found at level 46-47 on Thurbin Island in Erythia Sea.
Agnus Duoblade Elites (Japanese: , Agunusu Haiasaruto) are Minor Enemies in . They are Agnus Soldiers, and can be found at level 45-46 on Thurbin Island in Erythia Sea.
Agnus Vanguard Elites (Japanese: , Agunusu Haibangādo) are Minor Enemies in . They are Agnus Soldiers, and can be found at level 46-48 at Thurbin Island and Erythia Relay Base in Erythia Sea.
Aero Burst (Japanese: , Earobāsuto) is a Battle Art in . It is an Art of the Sharpshooter class, usable only by Mwamba. He fires a three-shot burst that fly through the air towards enemies.
Agnus Emblems are Normal Minor Enemies in . They are Agnian Standards, and can be found at level 46 at the Moonbright Regiment Outpost on the Aurora Shelf. They drop rare Emblem Adornments.
Agnus High Scouts are normal enemies in . They are Agnus Soldiers, and are fought at level 28-29 on The Ragmos Desolation and at level 47 at the Moonbright Regiment Outpost on the Aurora Shelf.

Amethyst Vanillas (Japanese: , Ameshisuto Ōnira) are collectables in . They can be found in Valak Mountain. According to their description, they are strongly sour vegetables people use to warm up that are available in cold lands and taste OK.
Angry Monkeys (Japanese: , Ikari Monkī) are collectables in . They can be found at Prison Island. According to their description, they have an angry-looking face but are in fact gentle natured.

The Antol Den (Japanese: , Antoru no nedoko) is a location in . It is located on Valak Mountain, near the Hollow Bone, exactly on top of the Nopon Camp. In the tunnel, across a chasm and an ice bridge, a small platform can be seen above the exit corridor. The Banquet Vassago and the Barbaric Sitri can both be fought here.

Andos (Japanese: , Andosu) are machine enemies in and . They are mainly found in Eryth Sea and in High Entia Tomb. They are floating machines created by the High Entia as defense units to protect Alcamoth and other places from intruders, especially Mechon. A pair protect the Cylinder Hangar in Colony 9. Later on, when the armies of Bionis march to Sword Valley, there are numerous Andos flying around in battle with the Mechon.

Aora Telethia (Japanese: , Aoro Tereshia) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are Drakos-type members of the Telethia family, and can be found at locations around Eryth Sea, such as Soltnar Seal Island, after the events at Mechonis Core. A variant also appears at Alcamoth at a slightly higher level and with different treasure drops.

The Apis Lair (Japanese: , Apisu no sumika) is a location in . It is located on Valak Mountain to the north of the Zokhed Pass and the Serik Waterfall. As its name suggests, it is populated by Apis, which can drop Apis Gold Nuggets, needed for Material Quest 3. It can be reached by taking the second ramp on the right north of Zokhed Pass.

Ansel Fish Pies are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by Ansels on Valak Mountain, or traded with Kurralth when he is in the Harict Chapel after the events of Mechonis Core. According to their description, they are prepared by seven cooks in unison, which is considered a dangerous kitchen. The party is tasked to collect three of these in A Gift For Miko.

The Arena (Japanese: , Tōgijō) is a location in . It is located on floor 3F of Prison Island, and only accessible on the second visit. When the party first enters the Arena, Dickson seals the exit and sets the Obelis Obart on them. After defeating it, the floor drops down a level into the Battle Arena on 2F, and the Demon Pavlovsk enters from the Behemoth Nest which the party must defeat. Upon leaving the Battle Arena, the story quest Chase Dickson is activated, and the party must make their way back to the Arena and fight the Master Obart. Defeating this third enemy causes a ramp to emerge from a wall, allowing the party to reach the Empty Throne and a transporter to the Great Canyon.

Apex Lake (Japanese: , Teppen no Mizūmi) is a location in . It is located on the eighth floor of Frontier Village. A Nopon guide here provides transport from Frontier Village to the Eryth Sea, and thus all of Upper Bionis. It is a round shining lake, with several grassy islands covered in flowers, with a fair number of Nopon NPCs on them, at least one of whom gives a quest. Berryjammy can be found here at night, and it is also the location of a Heart-to-Heart between Dunban and Melia - "True Natures".

Arel Telethia (Japanese: , Areru Tereshia) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are Phoenix-type members of the Telethia family, and can be found at level 86-87 throughout the Eryth Sea, including Latael Shore, the Hovering Reefs, and Central Seal Island, after the events at Mechonis Core. A variant also appears in Alcamoth at a slightly higher level and with different treasure drops. Both variants drop Rare Telethia Crystals, which can have Haste V on them. Arel Telethias are immune to Paralysis.

Antol Fire Pouches are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can only be dropped by Ent Antols on Valak Mountain and traded for. According to their description, they contain a liquid at over 200 degrees and they can be used to boil an egg instantly. Two are needed for The Freezing Nopon.

Apis Gold Nuggets are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are dropped by Apis on Valak Mountain and can be traded for with Zain. According to their description, they are pretty lumps of golden grains that are really just weathered Apis eggs. Five of them are needed for Material Quest 3 from Frontier Village. They are more commonly found at the Apis Lair.

Ardun Horns are rare materials in . They can only be dropped by Leg Arduns and Violent Andante on Bionis' Leg. Adurn Horns are otherwise not available. According to their description, they are symbols of strength that are always sounded before a major battle.

Antol Sleeping Bags are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by Pods on Valak Mountain, and can be traded for with Zain during either Adventurers in Peril or The Missing Partner. According to their description, they are sleeping bags which are warm and cosy, but makes the user smell of bugs when they wake up.

Archibolt, the Revolutionary (Japanese: , Kaiten no Āchiboruto) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Terebra family. It can be found at level 11 on an island in the southern part of Biahno Lake in Primordia during rainy weather. It must be defeated during the eponymous Basic Mission Archibolt, the Revolutionary.

Andrei, the Cunning (Japanese: , Kōkatsuna Andorei) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Caro family. It can be found at level 40 at Lower Delusian Mountains in Sylvalum. It must be defeated to complete the eponymous Basic Mission Andrei, the Cunning.

Aquatic Sacrifoles (Japanese: , Wōta Kurusuta) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Sacrifole family, and can be found at level 24-26 in Cauldros. They can be found at FN Site 515 disguised as flowers on the mountain walls and along the coastline at the end of the path leading down.

Appendage Fragments were items in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They were exclusively obtained by destroying the appendages of Nemesis enemies. These items are now unobtainable after the shutdown of Wii U online services. While the Nemesis mission remained available, Appendage Fragments could be sold for Credits via the Inventory, or exchanged for Reward Tickets via the Global Nemesis Battle Spoils option at the Network Console. If the Nemesis was defeated, one type of Appendage Fragment was randomly chosen to be converted to a very rare material specific to that enemy, and the rest were converted to Reward Tickets. If the Nemesis fled without being defeated, all Appendage Fragments from that enem

The Antimatter-R is a superweapon for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It consists of two parts attached to the back. When in use, the Skell connects the two parts to form a long range rifle that fires a single powerful shot.
is a Skell frame antidamage augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It prevents GP loss and boosts GP by 50 to 250 when an appendage is destroyed.

Anchor Shot (Japanese: , Ankāshotto) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Rex's arts when wielding the Aegis Sword. When using this salvager's unique Art, Rex fires his anchor at the enemy, causing one or more HP Potions to drop that restore Health to all of his allies, before swinging his sword leftward. The player can choose to preserve this for a pinch or use it immediately as necessary. During the battle against the Rampaging Ardun, Anchor Shot gains the ability to inflict Topple if the first hit connects, due to Vandham teaching Rex how to use his anchor to topple an enemy.

This page lists all the quests available in the Argentum Trade Guild. The list may be viewed in the order they become available or the order they appear in the Quest Log. Some quests require certain Blades to be acquired or leveled up. Due to the nature of unlocking Blades, it may be difficult to do all of these quests as soon as the chapter requirement is met. If a quest requires a specific Blade, it will be noted. Terms and abbreviations are explained in the legend at the bottom of the page. |-|Availability Order= This table is divided into sections based on the point in the story at which they become available (if other prerequisites are met). Ancient Star Compasses are Treasure items in . They can be obtained through Salvaging at Jubilee Gate at the Cliffs of Morytha. One is needed during Souvenirs from Morytha.

Angrite Chips are Core Chips in . All weapons forged with a Spiral Chip deal 50% more damage against Titans. They can be obtained after completing Farewell, Good Friend, or can be dropped by Relentless Arduran, Beast-Hunter William, Unflinching Saxton, and Gefillon Behemoths. Between Angrite Chips, Winonaite Chips and Spiral Chips, Angrite Chips have the highest Critical rate, only superseded by Sunlight Chips and then Moon Matter Chips. Angrite Chips share their appearance with Aubrite Chips, Howardite Chips, and Nakhlite Chips. __TOC__

Antique Judgment is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Empire of Mor Ardain from Tully in the Admar Storage Zone, when the nation has at least 2 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 50 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 12 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Keen Eye", "Focus" and "Ancient Wisdom" Field Skills.

Anagra Riiks (Japanese: , Anagura Ratōru) are enemies in . They are members of the Riik family and can be found at level 3-4 on the Upper Level of the Gormott Province. They have a chance of spawning when a Gorian Buloofo with low HP uses the "Beast Howl" ability. This enemy drops no items.

Ankl Tirkin (Japanese: , Āche Tākin) are two Quest Exclusive Enemies in . They are members of the Tirkin family, and can be found at level 42 along with two Pilum Tirkin on Daram Isle in the Leftherian Archipelago, then at the Goldmouth Flight Deck in the Argentum Trade Guild applying assistance to the Tirkin King during the Quest Birds of a Feather.

Ardainian Cetus (Japanese: , Superubia Shumiddo) are Quest Exclusive Enemies in . They are small flying Titan weapons piloted by Ardainian Soldiers, and can be found at level 43–45 around Hardhaigh Dock, Lv. 2 in the Empire of Mor Ardain during the Blade Quest Newt Recruits. Defeating them is not required for the quest.

Arach-no-More is a DLC Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Kingdom of Tantal automatically after clearing the DLC Quest Merclibay's Mightiest. The time required to complete this mission is 30 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 7 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Superstrength" and "Expeditionist" Field Skills. It uniquely awards more Trust Points than other normal Merc Missions. Completing this mission will unlock the DLC Merc Mission Showdown at Chilsain.

The Ardainian Sharper (Japanese: , Superubia Sunaipā) is a Challenge Battle Enemy in . They are an Ardainian Soldier who is fought at level 104 during the Challenge Battle 9th Imp. Armored Div.. This enemy drops no items. This specific type of Soldier appears to be some kind of Sniper. Its auto-attacks have long range; it is also six times more powerful than a normal Ardainian Soldier's auto-attack, inflicts Knockback and drains a full section of the Party Gauge. Due to its high dexterity, and a specific stat on its auto-attack, the Ardainian Sharper is very unlikely to miss.

Appearance is an equipment option in . Obtaining a weapon or Armour unlocks its appearance. This unlock is permanent across all save files, including , and does not require the game to be saved after obtaining it. The player can buy a piece of equipment and reload an earlier save to gain the appearance. The ability to set an appearance for Shulk's weapon is restricted until the player has beaten the game at least once, and is only available in New Game +. In , the player is instead required to have beaten this epilogue story at least once.
The Antol Pit (Japanese: , Antoru no Shin'en) is a location in . It is located on Corne Island in Erythia Sea. The Unique Monster Spiky Aurelia can be found here.

Archbow Gulkins are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Gulkin family, and can be found at level 47 on Daedal Isle and Corne Island, level 75 on Lavi Sandbar, and level 98 in the Malevolent Hollow in Erythia Sea.

Archpike Gulkins are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Gulkin family, and can be found at level 47 on Daedal Isle and Corne Island, level 74 on Lavi Sandbar, and level 96-97 in the Demihuman Gutter in Erythia Sea.

Aqua Mind is a Battle Art in . It is an art of the Lifesage class. Aqua Mind is unlocked as a Master Art upon achieving Rank 10 with the class. When used, the user assumes a stance that allows nearby allies to be healed at the rate of 25% of the user's Healing Power every second, in addition to increasing allies' recharge speed by 25% (this cannot stack).

The Argan Cathedral Ruins (Japanese: , Daishinden Āgen Iseki) is a Location in . It is located on the Black Mountains. It is the ruins of a structure from the Kingdom of Tantal. An Ether Lift must be constructed to get past the ruins, as the large door in the back of the ruins cannot be opened. The Alabaster Throne and Kana Peak are located behind the ruins. The ruins are initially occupied by seventeen Ignas, which must be defeated to capture the territory. To the northwest of the ruins, there is a broken lute on the ground that, when collecting it, begins the quest A Melody Sustained. The Ancient Rooftop Camp (Japanese: , Kyūshigai Iseki no Kyūsokuchi) is a Rest Spot in . It is located on a rooftop at the Town of Banerro Ruins on the Black Mountains. It can be reached using an Ether Slide. Cathy can be found here.

Amryn is an NPC in . She is a City Survivor who can be found near the Old Legre-Bhaja Battlefront on the Aurora Shelf. She moves to Colony 9 once rescued. Amryn's Community is gained when talking to her after changing Axel and Finley's Community status and talking with her three times.
Annie is an NPC in . She is a City Survivor found in the Ragrinar Passage on the Aurora Shelf. After being rescued from monsters, she passes away due to her injuries.
The Ares's Cores are important objects in . They are six cores used to power the Ares Prime.

Armoured Rockwell (Japanese: , Kōkaku no Rokkuweru) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Torta family, and can be found at level 82 on Bionis' Leg under Viliera Hill only during rainstorms or thunderstorms. It can drop the Immortal Moss needed for Replica Monado 2.

Attack Plus (Japanese: , Kōgekiryoku Kyōka) is a Gem in and that increases the maximum Attack of weapons. Increasing a weapon's maximum Attack will also increase the maximum damage for Auto-Attacks, Talent, Physical and Ether Arts, but will have no effect on Healing Arts. Due to a quirk in programming, the actual damage inflicted by a weapon cannot exceed its minimum + 99. As a result, weapons with a large difference between minimum and maximum damage may receive little or no benefit from this gem, unless the minimum attack is also raised by use of Attack Stability gems. This quirk has been fixed in the , and the issue does not happen anymore.

Attack Stability (Japanese: , Kōgekiryoku Antei) is a Gem in that increases the minimum Attack of weapons. This affects the amount of Damage done by Auto-Attacks, talent arts, physical arts and ether arts. It does not affect the amount of HP recovered by healing arts. __TOC__

Attack V Goggles (Japanese: , Atakku V Gōguru) are Mechonis goggles in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are part of the Attack V set for Fiora, along with the Attack V Frame, Attack V Arms, and Attack V Boosters. They can be obtained from Glory and Gloria Slobos on Valak Mountain. Attack V Goggles are not otherwise available.

Atomis Ansels are enemies in . They are members of the Ansel family, and can be found during the day at level 45 – 46 on the lower level of Valak Mountain. In particular, several Atomis Ansels can be found near Bionis' Wrist, southeast of a narrow path with three Krawli Slobos, as well as along the path between Jakt Geyser and the Sealed Tower. They can drop Ansel Fish Pies, which are required for A Gift For Miko.

The Ascension Hall (Japanese: 聖天翔の間, Shōtenshō no Ma) is a landmark in . It is located in the Imperial Palace in Alcamoth. It can be reached by walking east from the Great Hall, and contains a teleporter leading to a point between the Sky Terrace and the Audience Chamber on the second floor. A Heart-to-Heart - "The Forefathers" - is located here.
